description: Recorded real-data fixtures for the severe-storm meteorological detector cluster. Nothing in this directory is synthetic or hand-edited: every file is the verbatim HTTP response body recorded from the named public endpoint at the named UTC instant.

nws_severe_thunderstorm_warnings.json.content: 25 real NWS Severe Thunderstorm Warnings (most recent at record time), CAP GeoJSON with Impact-Based Warning parameters including maxHailSize (values such as '1.00', '0.75', 'Up to .75'), hailThreat, maxWindGust.
nws_severe_thunderstorm_warnings.json.notes: Used by the hail detector NWS cross-check wiring tests.

nws_dust_storm_warnings.json.content: 5 real NWS Dust Storm Warnings issued 2026-07-08 for the San Luis Valley, Colorado (Alamosa/Conejos/Costilla/Huerfano/Saguache counties).
nws_dust_storm_warnings.json.notes: Used by the dust-storm detector NWS cross-check wiring tests, and as a schema-identical populated CAP feed for the winter detector's negative-filter test.

nws_winter_alerts_query_july.json.content: Real (verbatim) NWS API response: an empty FeatureCollection. The api.weather.gov /alerts retention window does not reach back to the previous northern-hemisphere winter, so a July query for Winter Storm Warnings genuinely returns zero features.
nws_winter_alerts_query_july.json.notes: Committed as-recorded rather than fabricating a winter alert payload. The winter detector's populated-feed filtering behaviour is exercised against the schema-identical real dust/severe-thunderstorm fixtures above (the CAP property schema is shared across NWS products); this file exercises the honest empty-feed path.

spc_hail_archive_subset.csv.method: GET; archive member 1955-2023_hail.csv extracted; rows filtered to the three HailLoader ground-truth event windows (2010-07-22..24, 2016-04-10..13, 2017-05-07..09) plus the verbatim header
spc_hail_archive_subset.csv.content: 451 verbatim rows of the NOAA SPC severe-hail report archive (schema om,yr,mo,dy,date,time,tz,st,stf,stn,mag,...; mag = hail diameter in inches): 69 rows for the 2010 Vivian SD record-hailstone window (max mag 8.00), 238 rows for the April 2016 Texas hail outbreak (max 5.25), 144 rows for the May 2017 Colorado Front Range hailstorm (max 2.75).
spc_hail_archive_subset.csv.notes: Row selection by date window only; no row is edited. Used by the offline HailLoader tests in tests/loaders/test_hail_loader.py.

spc_storm_reports_20120629.csv.content: Verbatim NOAA Storm Prediction Center filtered storm reports for the convective day 2012-06-29 12:00 UTC through 2012-06-30 11:59 UTC: 675 wind reports (plus tornado and hail sections), covering the historic 29 June 2012 Ohio Valley / mid-Atlantic derecho (the 'June 2012 North American derecho'). Speeds are mph where measured ('UNK' otherwise); times are HHMM UTC with values before 1200 belonging to 2012-06-30.
spc_storm_reports_20120629.csv.notes: The derecho regression test selects the derecho's report chain from this file using the corridor and timing published in the NOAA/NWS Service Assessment 'The Historic Derecho of June 29, 2012' (states IA/IL/IN/MI/OH/KY/WV/VA/MD/DC/DE/NJ/PA/NC, 16:00 UTC Jun 29 - 07:00 UTC Jun 30). The selection is documented test logic over unmodified real reports; no report is fabricated or altered.
